rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reflecting on the universe opens the way to true knowledge and understanding the divine; the Qur’an seeks to awaken this capacity in people.
rows.anchor: it is this reflection due to which the doors to true knowledge and to the comprehension of the divine are opened.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A phrase meaning “so that you embark on it” is elided before “so that you seek”; the conjunction signals the omission.
rows.anchor: The particle of copulation is indicating this suppression.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wonders of the sea should prompt gratitude, yet people set up and worship deities for seas and oceans.
rows.anchor: people should have been grateful to God; but these naïve people have set up deities for seas and oceans and have started to worship them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Classical Arabic leaves recoverable components unspoken in the constructions about paths and landmarks; the translation supplies the omitted wording.
rows.anchor: Some components are suppressed here in accordance with a linguistic style of classical Arabic. They have been expressed in the translation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God placed mountains on earth to maintain its balance.
rows.anchor: God has planted mountains in the earth which maintain its balance.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made canals flow through the earth, benefiting human beings.
rows.anchor: He has made canals to flow in it which are beneficial for human beings.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made paths so people could travel between places.
rows.anchor: paths in the earth so that people can travel from one place to anofther.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Landmarks help people recognize paths and find their way.
rows.anchor: to recognize these paths, He has fixed various landmarks so that people can assess them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stars guide desert travellers at night and also help measure time.
rows.anchor: The stars that glow in the night sky guide those who travel in the deserts and also are a means of measuring time.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These created blessings imply that worship is due to God rather than deities that created none of them.
rows.anchor: should He be worshipped or other deities who have not created any of these things?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse directs readers to the implications of monotheism and accountability in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: This verse directs attention to the consequences of belief in one God and in the accountability of the Hereafter.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idolaters acknowledged God as Creator yet shared His rights with creatures, thereby equating Creator and created.
rows.anchor: would make them share His rights and in this way equate the creator with His creatures.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite countless favors and ingratitude, God grants respite as Most Forgiving and Merciful so people can repent, amend, and become worthy of mercy rather than wrath.
rows.anchor: He gave them respite because He is Most Forgiving and Merciful. He wants them to benefit from this respite and repent and make amends

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse warns that respite is temporary: everything will be exposed, the smallest deeds counted, and justice administered.
rows.anchor: A day will come when everything would be exposed. The smallest of deeds will be taken into consideration and justice shall be administered.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People know God gave them these favors but feign ignorance: their hearts believe while their tongues deny it.
rows.anchor: their hearts believe but their tongues lie.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first verse concerns baseless deities: they are themselves created and have created nothing, making their worship foolish.
rows.anchor: those whom they worship are themselves created and have created nothing. Worshipping them is foolishness.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next verse concerns worshipped forefathers, who are dead and do not know when resurrection will occur; calling on the dead is pointless.
rows.anchor: their forefathers they worship are dead and do not even know when they would be raised to life. What is the point of calling the dead?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description “not alive” emphasizes the noun “the dead.”
rows.anchor: not alive) is meant to emphasize the noun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The underlying reality is not hidden from these people.
rows.anchor: The implication of this verse is that the actual reality is not hidden from these

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their resistance concerns personal honor and arrogance rather than truth: long practice makes them unwilling to discredit ancestral worship through words or by abandoning it.
rows.anchor: the question does not relate to truth or falsehood. It relates to their personal honour that smacks of arrogance

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows their hearts are arrogant; this trait drives their deliberate denial of truth and persistence in evil, and God hates such people.
rows.anchor: It is due to this detestable trait they are deliberately denying the truth and intentionally adhering to evil. God hates such arrogant and conceited people.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verses 24–32 describe arrogant opponents’ schemes to shield followers from Qur’anic influence, then the fates of both groups, contrasting the righteous advocates of the Qur’an and their rewards in this life and the next.
rows.anchor: They would indulge in this foul play to stop people under their influence from being impacted by the message of the Qur’ ān.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who split the prophets’ religion or adulterate monotheism with polytheism bear responsibility for the corruption; the prophets are absolved.
rows.anchor: These prophets are absolved from this.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Innovations splintered God’s religion into factions, each opposing the prophets’ religion to uphold its own ways; this is a threat to such people.
rows.anchor: These words sound a threat to the people who had marred God’s religion with innovation thus splitting it into pieces

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told to disregard his opponents, since God will expose their deeds when they return to Him.
rows.anchor: he should disregard these people who are opposing him because once they return to God, He will expose their deeds.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who do righteous deeds with faith will have their effort rewarded, with every virtue recorded and none of their deeds missed.
rows.anchor: Each and every virtue done by them would have been noted down and there is no possibility that any of their deeds is missed by God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God accepts only deeds done for Him in faith; deeds lacking that sincerity carry no weight, even if they involve migration or jihad.
rows.anchor: only those deeds are acceptable to God which are done only for Him while having faith in Him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūrah’s closing section resumes its opening warning about the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: Warning people of the Hereafter with which the sūrah began is taken up again here.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This return to the opening guides readers to the Qur’an’s coherence, a style found in most sūrahs; it restores the sūrah’s real purpose if its expanse obscures it.
rows.anchor: The benefit of this style is that if the real purpose of a sūrah is lost in its expanse, it is brought before the addressees once again.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A part of the verse is elliptical in Arabic and is supplied as the sense that the people will never turn back to truth.
rows.anchor: A part of this verse is suppressed according to common linguistic styles of Arabic.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb for destroying a settlement conveys a settled decision; Arabic can express a certain future event as already accomplished.
rows.anchor: when the certainty of an incident or matter is to be expressed, it is stated as if it has already happened.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb رجع means to withdraw from falsehood and turn toward truth.
rows.anchor: means “withdrawing from falsehood and turning towards the truth.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should not worry over Quraysh’s faith: like earlier destroyed peoples despite their prophets’ utmost efforts, these stubborn people will not believe, so their matter should be left to God; the sūrah made the same point in verse 6.
rows.anchor: in a similar way, it is now become impossible for these people to accept faith.
